This document outlines the 
major maintenance procedures 
P2, 
which must be performed 
every five years 
indicated by Y5 in the above title block.

The 
soot blower used for cleaning superheater, reheater, economizer tubes, and 
regenerative air heater baskets.

The first draft initiated by eng. Abdalla M. Abdalla, reviewed 
by directed by eng: Gamal Arafa, revised by quality control eng. Samir Abd el-Gelil 
at edec, accepted by general director eng. M. Abd el-salam, approved by eng: 
Michael Goerge: head sector of Ayoun Moussa Steam Power Station 2x320 MW, 
and certified by eng. Aly Mostafa Al Lethy EDEPC inspection and quality 
control head sector

items:
A work 
 permit must be issued, the qualified maintenance staff should carry the 
 suitable safety category

Safety fence with caution marks 
 surrounding the work area is required,
Wear your safety helmet, shoes ... etc

Isolate the 
 circuit breaker for the motor of this soot blower

Isolate the 
 electrical cable feeding of the motor of this 
 soot blower

The soot blower 
 must be isolated mechanically by closing suction and delivery valve
Complete maintenance tool set
Cleaning fluid, Manual puller,
Suitable lifting device Feeler gauge

Hammer,
 Air wrench

Run the carriage forward (a few inches) to provide a 
 working clearance between the bulkhead and the rear of the SG (solid gland)

Thread the SG out of the hub until the first locking 
 slot (total of 6) aligns with a locking notch (total of 4) in the rear of the 
 hub

Connect the motor power supply and return the 
 carriage to the rear stop position Precautions must be taken to avoid binding 
 with the poppet valve turn on linkage and/or hard stop the SG into the poppet 
 valve mounting hardware Open the blowing medium isolation valve and pressurize 
 the piping upstream of the poppet valve

Notify "Operations" that the soot blower will be 
 test run

Run the soot blower, check for leakage or other 
 problems Make corrections/repairs as required

If there is no leakage or other problems found, 
 notify "Operations" that the soot blower may be placed into normal service

sections.text:
It is recommended that complete packing set be replaced for maximum service 
 life, since the total packing set height for the 5 ring set (2 end rings and 3 
 seal rings) is 18" (4572 mm) and the SG can adjust for about 75" (1905 mm)

items:
Notify "Operations" that the soot blower is being removed from remote service 
 control

Isolate the Mowing medium upstream of the poppet valve and relieve any trapped 
 pressure Precautions should be taken to prevent any pressure buildup from an 
 upstream isolation valve

Disconnect the poppet valve turn on linkage and run the carriage forward 
 approximately 10-12 inches (254 mm - 3048 mm)
Disable the motor power supply
Remove the locking key from the SG
Using the spanner wrench, unthread the SG from the hub

disconnect the feed tube from the poppet valve and slide it towards the 
 carriage Do this until there is adequate clearance between the end of the feed 
 tube and bulkhead to remove the SG assembly and packing
Remove the SG assembly by sliding it off of the feed tube

If the packing set is only partially being replaced, remove the rear rings as 
 required The rear end ring must be replaced when adding rings Do not 
 damage/disturb the remaining rings or the front bushing

If the complete packing set is being replaced, remove the packing rings and 
 the front bushing The front bushing designed for use with the 5 ring packing 
 set has two threaded holes (#10-24 @ 180) for pulling the bushing from the 
 carriage hub

In some situations it may be necessary to support the hub end of the lance 
 tube and unbolt it from the carriage By doing this, the feed tube can be 
 pushed through the carriage hub to remove the front bushing and packing Also, 
 the hub is clear for cleaning

Remove the packing rings with a flexible packing hook Direct the hook to avoid 
 damaging the feed tube or hub bore

Clean the hub cavity packing bore and the internal threads to remove any 
 debris/residue A solvent may be required to remove all residue

Inspect the front bushing, the rear bushing and clean or replace as required 
 The rear bushing is lightly pressed into the SG

Slide the feed tube through the carriage hub and connect the lance flange to 
 the hub flange A new sealing gasket must always be used The feed tube may be 
 pulled by using a short piece of bar or tubing with an 0 D slightly smaller 
 than the feed tube I D The use of 0 D gripping devices can damage the 0 D 
 sealing surface

Install the front bushing over the feed tube (small pilot diameter towards 
 hub) and into the hub cavity The flat end of the packing tool assembly may be 
 used to seat the bushing at the hub shoulder It may help to slightly raise the 
 feed tube to pilot the bushing into the small hub bore If the bushing is not 
 seated in the hub properly, the packing and SG will be out of position

Remove any raised metal on the feed tube 0 D with crocus cloth over a file or 
 use a fine stone Check the end, mounting threads or snap ring groove, P/N and 
 logo marking

Before placing each section of the sealing ring packing over the feed tube, 
 place the I D of the conical ring over the thumbnail and while rotating the 
 packing slightly roll the sharp comer of the packing which first contacts the 
 feed tube Remember that the packing seal rings are conically pointed towards 
 the front busing This slightly increases the diameter and makes a nice 
 lead-in, and prevents damage of the packing I D

Slide each ring of packing (use proper sequence and bevel towards the front 
 bushing) to the full in position and seat it with 3 to 4 solid impacts of the 
 packing tool The bevel on the end of the packing tool must match the bevel of 
 the packing rings The split end rings must be installed with the single skive 
 cuts overlapping properly

Slide the SG over the feed tube and thread into the hub until it makes contact 
 with the packing Do not tighten

Connect the feed tube and poppet valve as directed in the soot blower 
 instruction manual A new sealing gasket, proper lubrication and proper 
 torquing must always be used

Using the spanner wrench, thread the SG into the hub until there is adequate 
 preload on the packing or use the spanner wrench with a torque wrench and 
 torque the gland to 180 in-lb (2033 NM) For specific torque instructions,

Thread the SG out of the hub until the first locking slot (total of 6) aligns 
 with a locking notch (total of 4) in the rear of the hub

Install the locking key using the ??10-32 screw and lock washer Make certain 
 the locking key is fully engaged in the notch of the hub before tightening the 
 screw

connect the motor supply and return the carriage to the rear stop position 
 Precautions must be taken to avoid binding with the poppet valve turn on 
 linkage and/or hard stop the SG into the poppet valve mounting hardware Open 
 the blowing medium isolation valve and pressurize the piping upstream of the 
 poppet valve
Notify "Operations" that the soot blower will be test run

Run the soot blower, check for leakage or other problems Make 
 corrections/repairs as required

If there is no leakage or other problems found, notify "Operations" that the 
 soot blower may be placed into normal service

sections.text:
Torquing of the solid gland requires the use of the spanner 
 wrench and torque wrench with a 1/2" drive The net torque value applied to the 
 solid gland is based on two factors:

The working length is a feature of the specific torque wrench design and is 
 not the actual physical length of the torque wrench

items:
The offset angle is that angle between the axis of the spanner wrench handle 
 and the axis of the torque wrench If the handle on the spanner wrench and the 
 torque wrench are in line, the offset angle is 0

The gland torque value of 180 in-lb (2033 NM) is based on a torque wrench 
 with a "working length" of 65 inches (1651 mm) with a 0 "offset angle" with 
 the spanner wrench handle

Solid Gland Torque Instructions
Torquing of the solid gland requires the use of the spanner

Working Wrench Length
The working length is a feature of the specific torque wrench design and is 
 not the actual physical length of the torque wrench
Offset Angle
